Definition: Security Information and Event Management -- a platform that collects, normalizes, stores, correlates, and alerts on security telemetry.
The flow of collection, normalization/enrichment, storage/indexing, correlation/detection, and alerting/dashboards.
Elastic Common Schema and Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework -- common normalization schemas for security telemetry.
Retention tiers from fast and expensive to slow and cheap, balancing query latency against cost.
Treating detection rules as software: version-controlled, peer-reviewed, tested, and lifecycle-managed.
A vendor-neutral YAML SIEM rule format with converters into specific SIEM query languages.
A pattern-matching rule language for identifying malware by file content.
Open network IDS signature languages widely shared by community and commercial feeds.
User and Entity Behavior Analytics -- behavioral baselining of users and entities to detect statistical anomalies.
A composite numerical score per entity that aggregates anomalies for analyst review.
Comparing a user's behavior against peers in the same role to surface deviations.
Proactive, hypothesis-driven search for adversaries already inside the environment.
A decoy system or network used to detect and study attacker activity with high signal-to-noise ratio.
A decoy secret whose use generates a high-confidence alert.
Collected and refined information about adversaries -- their tools, TTPs, infrastructure, and targets.
Open-Source Intelligence -- intelligence drawn from public feeds, reports, and analyses.
Information Sharing and Analysis Center -- a sector-specific threat-sharing community (FS-ISAC, H-ISAC, E-ISAC, MS-ISAC).
Structured Threat Information eXpression -- a JSON data model for threat intelligence.
Trusted Automated eXchange of Indicator Information -- an HTTPS REST transport for STIX bundles.
Threat Intelligence Platform -- a system that ingests, deduplicates, scores, ages, and operationalizes threat intelligence.
A four-tier layering of threat intelligence by audience and time horizon.
Indicator of Compromise -- an observable artifact (IP, domain, hash, URL, mutex) associated with malicious activity.
Mean Time To Detect / Mean Time To Respond -- the primary SOC effectiveness metrics.
The duration from initial compromise to detection -- the canonical measure of detective shortfall.
